findings.description: The class was renamed to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`, but the file and unchanged callers still import/construct `SelectedCalendarRepository`. The targeted repository suite now fails all 12 tests with `SelectedCalendarRepository is not a constructor`, and the same stale constructor is used while loading both calendar-subscription API routes. The repository mandate also requires the filename to exactly match the Prisma-prefixed class. Rename the file to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository.ts` and update the test plus both API routes to import and construct the new class.
findings.failureMode: Tests and runtime loading of the calendar-subscription cron/webhook routes fail because their imported constructor no longer exists.
findings.title: Rename the file and callers together with the repository class

findings.description: `@group.calendar.google.com` is also the suffix Google assigns to ordinary user-created secondary calendars, not just generic calendars. This repository documents adding such an ID as a selected calendar, while the subscription feature is described as covering all calendars. When that calendar belongs to a cache-enabled team, the new `endsWith` predicate permanently omits it from the subscription batch, so it never receives a sync token or webhook-backed cache and every availability read continues hitting Google. Remove this non-unique suffix from the generic suffix list; any shared-calendar exclusion must use metadata that actually distinguishes it.
findings.failureMode: A user selects a normal Google secondary calendar whose ID ends in @group.calendar.google.com; the subscription cron never subscribes it and cache/sync is silently disabled for that calendar.
findings.title: Do not classify every Google secondary calendar as generic

findings.description: The new `return True` references a nonexistent identifier. The required `type-check:tsgo` CI step fails with TS2304 whenever this file is compiled, so this PR cannot pass the web style job. Return `true` or omit the return value.
findings.failureMode: The required frontend type-check fails deterministically with TS2304 on the undefined `True` identifier.
findings.title: Use the JavaScript boolean literal in the schema handler

findings.description: This hunk deletes the only use of `const v = JSON.parse(value)` (the removed `properties: v`) but retains the assignment immediately before the changed line. The required web lint step reports `sonarjs/no-dead-store` as an error, so this PR cannot pass the style job. Invoke `JSON.parse(value)` only for validation without assigning it, or use the parsed result.
findings.failureMode: The required frontend lint check fails with `Remove this useless assignment to variable "v"` after this hunk makes `v` unused.
findings.title: Do not leave the parsed schema in a dead store

findings.description: `normalizedJsonSchema` is assigned here and never read; `payloadToSave` recomputes the same condition directly. The required web lint step reports this as a `sonarjs/no-dead-store` error, so this PR cannot pass the style job. Remove the variable or use it when constructing `payloadToSave`.
findings.failureMode: The required frontend lint check fails with a no-dead-store error for `normalizedJsonSchema`.
findings.title: Remove the unused normalized schema assignment

findings.description: Leaving the newly optional schema blank saves `json_schema: undefined`. Both workflow/chat editors submit a string, `_validate_inputs` validates it with `json.loads` but returns that string, and `StartNode._validate_and_normalize_json_object_inputs` immediately skips conversion when no schema is present. Thus `{"name":"Ada"}` remains a string even though the workflow type system exposes this input as `VarType.object`; downstream object access receives the wrong type. Parse and enforce an object for JSON_OBJECT values regardless of whether a validation schema is supplied.
findings.failureMode: Creating a JSON_OBJECT input with the optional schema left empty, then running with valid JSON, produces a string-valued workflow variable instead of an object and breaks downstream object access.
findings.title: Normalize schema-less JSON_OBJECT inputs

findings.description: `json_schema` is updated only after `JSON.parse(value)` succeeds. Monaco keeps an invalid value in its own model while the React payload remains the previous valid schema (or `undefined`), so clicking Confirm validates and saves that stale payload instead of reaching `jsonSchemaInvalid`, silently discarding the visible edit. Keep a raw schema draft on every change (and preserve it in the editor when parsing fails), then parse that draft during confirmation.
findings.failureMode: Entering malformed JSON in the newly enabled schema editor and confirming silently saves the old/no schema instead of showing the advertised invalid-schema error, discarding the user's edit.
findings.title: Keep invalid editor text so confirmation can reject it

findings.description: Enabling JSON in this selector makes switching back to `json_object` reachable, but `jsonSchemaStr` branches on `type` while its memo depends only on `tempPayload.json_schema`. For example, configure a JSON input with a schema, switch it to text and save (type changes do not clear the schema), reopen it as text, then select JSON here. The memo cached `''` while the type was text and does not rerun, so the editor appears empty even though confirmation silently retains the old schema. Add `type` to the memo dependencies.
findings.failureMode: After a JSON variable is temporarily saved as another type and changed back through the newly enabled selector, the editor displays blank while an old hidden schema remains active and unexpectedly validates workflow inputs.
findings.title: Recompute the schema display when switching to the newly enabled type

findings.description: The moved call now runs `setUpExperimentVariables()` only after `setUpApp()`. `FeatureFlaggedTestSuite.setUpApp()` immediately passes the implicitly-unwrapped `jsonFileName` and `featureName` to `addLaunchArgument`, so a concrete suite using this base traps on nil during setup instead of configuring its experiment. Restore `setUpExperimentVariables()` before `setUpApp()`.
findings.failureMode: Any test suite subclassing FeatureFlaggedTestSuite crashes in setup by force-unwrapping the still-nil feature variables.
findings.title: Initialize feature variables before consuming them

findings.description: `BaseTestCase.setUp()` is now `async throws`, but the iPad-only override calls it with only `await`. Swift rejects this exact XCTest override pattern with “call can throw but is not marked with 'try',” so the XCUITest target cannot compile; use `try await super.setUp()`.
findings.failureMode: Building the XCUITest target fails because a throwing async call is not marked `try`.
findings.title: Use `try` when awaiting the throwing superclass setup

findings.description: After `BaseTestCase` moves its lifecycle implementation to the async overloads, synchronous `forceRestartApp()` still calls `tearDown()` and `setUp()`. Swift resolves these to XCTest's separate synchronous methods (confirmed by SIL), so the helper no longer executes the changed methods that terminate/launch the app and rebuild the navigator. The authentication test therefore does not actually verify persistence across a restart. Make the helper and its callers async/throwing and use `try await`.
findings.failureMode: Tests using forceRestartApp observe no application restart because its synchronous calls bypass the newly async BaseTestCase setup and teardown implementations.
findings.title: Make the restart helper call the async lifecycle overrides

findings.description: This hunk deletes the required header lines `// This Source Code Form is subject to the terms of the Mozilla Public`, `// License, v. 2.0. If a copy of the MPL was not distributed with this`, and `// file, You can obtain one at http://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/`. A11yUtils.swift now starts with `import XCTest`, and the enabled `file_header` rule reports it. Restore the exact MPL header at the top.
findings.failureMode: The changed Swift file fails the enabled file-header lint/compliance check because its required top-of-file MPL notice was removed.
findings.title: Restore the required MPL header

findings.description: `openForm` remains optional, and `MainForm` renders `FormWrapper` without it. Once that composer is focused, `isOpen` becomes true and this dereference throws instead of rendering the open form; strict TypeScript also flags the line as TS18048. Retain optional chaining (or guard `openForm`).
findings.failureMode: Focusing the top-level comment form sets `isOpen` true while `openForm` is undefined, causing a render-time TypeError and breaking the primary composer.
findings.title: Preserve the optional open-form guard

findings.description: The effect now gates TipTap on `member.expertise`, although expertise is optional and the surrounding flow requires a member name. Thus a named member with no expertise gets a read-only composer and cannot submit; conversely, a member with expertise but no name gets the autofocus reply editor enabled and can bypass the name-details prompt. Gate on the current `memberName` (without the parent-comment fallback).
findings.failureMode: For `{name: 'Jane Replier', expertise: null}` the composer is read-only; for `{name: null, expertise: 'Some Expertise'}` an autofocus reply composer is enabled despite the mandatory name prompt.
findings.title: Gate editor access on the member name

findings.description: `parent` is the top-level comment that owns the reply list, while `openForm.in_reply_to_id` is populated with the specific reply the user selected. Replacing the latter with `parent.id` makes the server reject/clear the contextual reference because a top-level comment is not a reply under that parent. Replies to replies then lose their “Replied to” snippet/link and the selected reply's author notification; submit the target stored in `openForm`.
findings.failureMode: Clicking Reply on reply ID 2 under root ID 1 posts `in_reply_to_id: 1`; server parent validation clears the reference, so the result is a direct reply without the expected contextual link to ID 2.
findings.title: Keep the selected reply as the reply target

findings.description: The changed order `pr-2 mt-[-16px]` violates the comments UI's error-level `tailwindcss/classnames-order` rule, so the package lint target fails on this line. Restore the previous canonical `mt-[-16px] pr-2` order.
findings.failureMode: Running `yarn lint` in `apps/comments-ui` reports an error at reply-form.tsx:47 and exits unsuccessfully.
findings.title: Restore canonical Tailwind class order

findings.description: The newly added `interface TranslationMap` violates the repository's error-level `ts/consistent-type-definitions: ['error', 'type']` rule, so the registered frontend lint check fails on this file. Declare this map as a `type` instead.
findings.failureMode: Running the repository frontend ESLint check exits nonzero at `web/test/i18n-mock.ts:4`, blocking CI/merge.
findings.title: Replace the new interface with a type alias

findings.description: The centralized `t` mock now serializes `returnObjects` into a string instead of preserving the old array-valued behavior. A test that follows the new guidance and relies on the global mock to render `SelfHostedPlanItem/List` receives `"billing.plans.community.features:{\"returnObjects\":true}"`; the component then calls `features.map(...)` and the test crashes with `TypeError: features.map is not a function`. Handle `returnObjects` before building the suffix (returning an array/custom array), as the deleted setup branch did.
findings.failureMode: Any test rendering a component that consumes an object/array translation through the advertised global mock can crash rather than render.
findings.title: Preserve array results for `returnObjects`

findings.description: When the billing batch contains a plan that fails `SubscriptionPlan` validation (for example, one missing `expiration_date`), this branch inserts that tenant into a return value declared and consumed as `dict[str, SubscriptionPlan]`. The added unit test explicitly expects the invalid tenant to be absent, so it fails at `len(result) == 2`; production/cache callers can likewise receive and cache JSON `null`, then error when indexing the plan. Remove this assignment and continue past the invalid item.
findings.failureMode: A malformed plan in an otherwise successful billing response is returned and cached as `None`, failing the added unit test and causing downstream plan access to error.
findings.title: Skip invalid plans instead of returning `None`

findings.description: `SubscriptionPlan` is a `TypedDict`, whose class body may contain only type annotations. The required backend style workflow runs basedpyright, and the check now fails at this method with `TypedDict classes can contain only type annotations`, so the PR cannot pass CI. Remove this ignored runtime method (or use a normal/Pydantic model if behavior is required).
findings.failureMode: Running the required strict basedpyright check fails on the changed `__str__` definition, blocking validation of the backend.
findings.title: Remove the method from `SubscriptionPlan`

findings.description: This repository can initialize `redis_client` as `RedisCluster`, but the generated keys use tenant-specific hashes and therefore normally map to different slots. Redis Cluster rejects a multi-key `MGET` unless every key shares one slot; the broad handler then treats every request as a miss, so repeated bulk calls always hit billing and this cache provides no load reduction in supported cluster deployments. Use a cluster-aware per-slot/pipelined read, or deliberately add a common hash tag to the cache keys.
findings.failureMode: With `REDIS_USE_CLUSTERS` and at least two tenant IDs in different hash slots, every cache read raises a cross-slot error and falls back to the billing API, making the new cache nonfunctional and potentially overloading billing.
findings.title: Avoid cross-slot `MGET` in Redis Cluster mode

findings.description: Calling `scheduling.init()` without its required options makes post-scheduling evaluate `options.apiUrl` while `options` is undefined, so every normal Ghost boot rejects with a TypeError before services finish initializing. Restore the `{apiUrl: urlUtils.urlFor(...)}` argument.
findings.failureMode: On normal startup, `initServices()` reaches this call; `post-scheduling/index.js` reads `options.apiUrl` and throws because `options` is undefined, leaving Ghost in maintenance/startup failure.
findings.title: Pass the required API URL to the scheduler

findings.description: The same hunk deletes `slack.listen()` even though only XML-RPC is being removed. No remaining production caller registers Slack's `post.published` or `slack.test` listeners, so configured Slack webhooks no longer receive publication notifications and the Slack test endpoint emits an event with no consumer. Restore `slack.listen()` in service initialization.
findings.failureMode: After startup (once the scheduler call is repaired), a site with a configured Slack webhook publishes a post or requests a Slack test; the event is emitted but no Slack listener was registered, so no webhook request is sent.
findings.title: Restore Slack event listener registration

findings.description: This new dependency-install note violates the repository's Yarn-v1-only package-management contract. A contributor following it runs npm inside the Yarn workspace, which can create an unsupported `package-lock.json` and install a dependency without updating the workspace's authoritative `yarn.lock`, causing non-reproducible local/CI dependency resolution. Change the command to `yarn add <package>`.
findings.failureMode: When a contributor adds a service dependency by following this boot-file instruction, npm mutates a different lockfile/install state than the repository's required Yarn v1 workflow, so the dependency can be absent or resolve differently in CI.
findings.title: Do not direct contributors to npm

findings.description: `bookingUrl` is initialized to an empty string, but `setBookingUrl` is never called when `getEventTypeById` returns the event type (Biome also identifies the setter as unused). Consequently, every existing event type hits the new “Booking URL not available” guard, so Preview and Copy stop working and `BasicsTab` never displays the API-provided organization URL. Set this state from `eventType.bookingUrl` in `applyEventTypeData`.
findings.failureMode: Open an existing event type whose API response includes `bookingUrl`, then press Preview or Copy; the permanently empty state triggers the error instead of opening/copying the URL.
findings.title: Populate the detail screen's booking URL

findings.description: The newly added `catch (error)` never reads `error`, and Biome reports `lint/correctness/noUnusedVariables` on this changed line. The exact base service passes lint, but the head now exits nonzero; remove this unnecessary try/catch and let `getUserProfile()`'s original error propagate.
findings.failureMode: Run Biome lint on `companion/services/calcom.ts`; it exits nonzero on line 1659, blocking the repository lint/pre-commit check.
findings.title: Remove the dead error wrapper

findings.description: The changed assignment is no longer in the repository's Biome format. The exact base file passes the formatter, while the head formatter exits nonzero and rewrites this hunk back to a same-line template-literal assignment, so the formatting check cannot pass until this changed code is formatted.
findings.failureMode: Run the repository's Biome formatter check on `content.ts`; it exits nonzero because of the changed lines 1125-1128.
findings.title: Restore Biome formatting in the copy handler

findings.description: This added call executes from `EventManager.collect` on the dedicated `GraphDispatcher` thread, which does not receive the Flask context preservation configured for worker threads. The concrete updater evaluates Flask-SQLAlchemy's `db.engine` only here, so every normal conversation-variable assignment raises “Working outside of application context”; the layer framework then logs and swallows the error and nothing is persisted. Inject a context-independent engine/session factory captured in the application context, or preserve an application context for this callback.
findings.failureMode: Any advanced-chat Variable Assigner invokes the updater on GraphDispatcher without Flask application context, so the persistence operation raises and the next turn sees the old value.
findings.title: Do not run the Flask-bound updater on GraphDispatcher

findings.description: The persistence write was moved from the node into `GraphEngineLayer.on_event`, but `EventManager._notify_layers` catches and only logs every exception raised by a layer. Consequently, a missing row, transient query failure, or commit failure at this call still leaves the Variable Assigner and graph marked successful while the database retains the old value; the next conversation turn silently loses the acknowledged update. This persistence path needs a failure/retry mechanism that can affect execution rather than relying on an exception from `on_event`.
findings.failureMode: A database error during a successful Variable Assigner event is logged by EventManager but the workflow returns success; reloading the conversation restores the stale variable value.
findings.title: Do not swallow conversation-variable write failures

findings.description: For a Variable Assigner inside an Iteration node, its success event can be dispatched by the outer engine before `IterationNode` copies the iteration snapshot back into the parent pool. This layer then re-reads the selector from the outer `graph_runtime_state` and writes the pre-iteration value, even though `item.new_value` contains the successful update; after snapshot synchronization there is no second assigner event. Under that reachable scheduling, the assignment appears updated during the run but reloads with the old value on the next turn. Persist from the emitting subgraph/event state (or install the persistence mechanism on that subgraph) rather than looking up the parent pool here.
findings.failureMode: An advanced-chat workflow updates a conversation variable from inside an Iteration node; the layer writes the parent's old value and the update is lost on the next conversation turn.
findings.title: Persist the variable from the emitting iteration state

findings.description: `update()` now constructs a bare `Session` instead of retaining the previous `with Session(...)` scope. If the selected conversation-variable row is missing (or the query/commit raises), the method exits without closing or rolling back the checked-out session; repeated failed updates can exhaust the database pool and make subsequent requests fail. Use the repository-mandated session context manager so every path releases the session.
findings.failureMode: A stale/missing conversation-variable ID or database exception leaves the new Session unclosed; repeated layer invocations exhaust DB connections and cause request failures.
findings.title: Close the updater's SQLAlchemy session

findings.description: The static dictionary strongly roots every accessor expression. Razor accessor trees contain captured constants such as the owning page/component, and each rerender or new request produces distinct expression objects; after disposal these keys remain forever (except on a hot-reload delta). The repository's FieldIdentifier parser explicitly avoids this pattern because accessors embed captured values. This leaks complete component graphs on every use and can exhaust a long-running server; worse, the changed account templates pass `Input.Password`, so an interactive page instance later populated with a user's password remains reachable from this static cache after navigation. Parse directly or cache only stable metadata without retaining expression/closure instances.
findings.failureMode: Using DisplayName across repeated renders/requests causes unbounded process memory growth and retains disposed account-page models, including entered passwords.
findings.title: Do not root accessor closures process-wide

findings.description: The render is skipped solely because the `Expression` instance is unchanged, but `DisplayAttribute.GetName()` is intentionally recomputed for culture-sensitive resources (the MVC metadata tests explicitly verify this). If an app stores the accessor in a field, changes `CurrentUICulture`, and rerenders the parent, Blazor resupplies the same accessor and this branch suppresses both lookup and rendering, leaving the old-language label. The same guard defeats the renderer's forced hot-reload parameter update for a stable accessor after a Display attribute edit. Re-evaluate/render the display name when parameters are supplied, or invalidate this component for culture/metadata changes.
findings.failureMode: A resource-backed DisplayName passed through a stable expression remains stale after an in-place culture change or metadata hot reload.
findings.title: Re-evaluate resource-backed names when parameters are resupplied

findings.description: This newly added C# file declares a block-scoped namespace, violating the repository's mandatory file-scoped namespace rule. The source therefore fails the repository's stated compliance criteria until the declaration is changed to `namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Forms;` and the wrapper braces are removed.
findings.failureMode: Repository compliance failure on the new public component source.
findings.title: Use the mandated file-scoped namespace

findings.description: `SupportsLocalizationWithResourceType` has no `// Arrange`, `// Act`, or `// Assert` phase comments, and the new `DisplayNameReadsAttributesCorrectly` test in `src/Components/test/E2ETest/Tests/FormsTest.cs` likewise uses only descriptive comments. These methods fail the repository's mandatory test-structure compliance; add the explicit phase markers to both tests.
findings.failureMode: The newly added tests fail the repository's mandatory AAA-comment compliance criteria.
findings.title: Add required Arrange-Act-Assert markers to new tests

findings.description: All seven new test methods that return `Task`, plus `RenderAndGetOutput`, omit the repository-mandated `Async` suffix (lines 14, 38, 61, 84, 107, 132, 157, and 177). Rename them consistently so the new test source meets the async API naming contract.
findings.failureMode: The newly added async methods fail the repository's mandatory async-naming compliance criteria.
findings.title: Suffix the new asynchronous methods with Async

findings.description: The new DTO import is unused and `@calcom/platform-types` does not depend on or resolve `@calcom/features`. Building that workspace now fails with TS2307 at this line before the API can build; remove the import.
findings.failureMode: `yarn workspace @calcom/platform-types build` fails with TS2307, blocking API build/deployment.
findings.title: Remove the undeclared BookingRepository import

findings.description: `getRecordings` is async, but the changed line stores its Promise and returns that Promise as `data`. Type-checking reports TS2740 because the Promise does not satisfy `RecordingItem[]`; if emitted anyway, JSON serialization produces `{}` instead of the recordings. Restore the deleted `await`.
findings.failureMode: The API build fails at the recordings response assignment; transpile-only execution would return `data: {}` to authorized callers.
findings.title: Await the recordings service result

findings.description: Nest evaluates method guards in list order, but this route invokes `BookingPbacGuard` before `ApiAuthGuard`. The PBAC guard reads `request.user` and immediately throws `UnauthorizedException` when it is absent, so the bearer token is never authenticated. The newly enabled organizer test expecting 200 will receive 401. Put `ApiAuthGuard` first, as on the other protected video routes.
findings.failureMode: Every normally authenticated organizer request to the transcripts endpoint is rejected with 401 before its credentials are processed.
findings.title: Authenticate before the transcript PBAC guard

findings.description: The recordings route is read-only and the analogous transcripts/conferencing routes require `BOOKING_READ`, but this changed decorator requires the distinct `BOOKING_WRITE` bit. `PermissionsGuard` performs an exact bitwise permission check, so a managed OAuth client provisioned for booking reads is incorrectly denied this authorized GET. Restore `BOOKING_READ`.
findings.failureMode: A managed OAuth client with the BOOKING_READ bit but not BOOKING_WRITE receives 403 when reading recordings for a booking it is otherwise authorized to access.
findings.title: Require booking-read for the recordings GET

findings.description: Both newly protected routes declare `booking.readRecordings`, but `BookingPbacGuard` never reads that metadata. It delegates to `doesUserIdHaveAccessToBooking`, whose PBAC team path checks the distinct `booking.readTeamBookings` permission. Because `readRecordings` depends only on `booking.read`, a custom role correctly granted recording access but not team-wide booking access is newly rejected by both routes. Make the booking-aware guard evaluate the declared recording permission after resolving the booking context, while retaining owner/host access.
findings.failureMode: On a PBAC-enabled team, a custom role explicitly granted booking.readRecordings receives 403 from the newly protected recordings and transcripts endpoints unless it also has the unrelated booking.readTeamBookings permission.
findings.title: Honor readRecordings in the booking PBAC guard

findings.description: When `TAURI_BUNDLER_TOOLS_GITHUB_MIRROR` is set, deleting `cdn.set_path(github_url);` makes this return only the configured mirror base. A GitHub-hosted WiX/NSIS/AppImage download therefore requests the mirror root instead of the asset and bundling fails (or receives unrelated data that fails verification/extraction). It also leaves `github_url` unused, so the warnings-denied Clippy job fails. Restore composition of the source URL/path onto the mirror base.
findings.failureMode: Set TAURI_BUNDLER_TOOLS_GITHUB_MIRROR=https://mirror.example.com and trigger a GitHub-hosted tool download; the generated URL is https://mirror.example.com/ rather than the mirrored asset URL.
findings.title: Preserve the asset path in base-mirror URLs

findings.description: The offline WebView2 GET was changed from `download(url)` to `ureq::get(url)`, bypassing `base_ureq_agent`. With platform-certs enabled, the preceding HEAD can succeed through a TLS-inspecting corporate/system CA, but this GET still uses ureq's ordinary root configuration and fails, so offline Windows bundling cannot download WebView2. Perform this request through the configured base agent (or the shared download helper).
findings.failureMode: On a network whose HTTPS chain is trusted only through the OS certificate store, webview2_guid_path's HEAD succeeds but downloading an uncached offline installer returns a certificate error.
findings.title: Use the platform-certificate agent for the installer GET

findings.description: The new base agent is selected only by `unwrap_or`, so when either GitHub mirror variable produces an alternative URL, `generate_github_alternative_url` still returns `ureq::agent()` and bypasses the platform verifier. A mirror whose TLS certificate is trusted by the OS (the exact corporate/proxied environment this feature supports) still fails tool downloads. Construct the mirror tuple with `base_ureq_agent()` as well.
findings.failureMode: Configure TAURI_BUNDLER_TOOLS_GITHUB_MIRROR_TEMPLATE to an HTTPS mirror signed by a system-installed private CA and trigger a GitHub tool download; the Some branch uses default WebPKI roots and returns a TLS certificate error.
findings.title: Apply platform certificates to mirror downloads too

findings.description: The new function ends with `return agent;`, which triggers Clippy's warn-by-default `needless_return` lint. Because this repository runs Clippy with warnings denied, the required lint job fails for the bundler; make `agent` the tail expression instead.
findings.failureMode: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; Clippy emits `needless_return` at this new line and exits unsuccessfully.
findings.title: Remove the needless explicit return so Clippy passes

findings.description: This field is the `tauri` runtime crate version used by `tauri init`, not the Rust CLI version: `init.rs` formats `metadata.tauri` directly into the generated dependency. This release leaves the `tauri` crate and changelog at 2.9.2 and has no Tauri change file, so a freshly initialized project from CLI 2.9.3 requests the unreleased `tauri ^2.9.3` and Cargo cannot resolve it. Only `cli.js.version` should be bumped here; leave `tauri` at 2.9.2.
findings.failureMode: Immediately after publishing this CLI-only release, `tauri init` generates a Cargo.toml requiring tauri 2.9.3 even though this release does not publish that crate, so the generated app fails dependency resolution.
findings.title: Keep runtime metadata at the published Tauri version

findings.description: When either `TAURI_BUNDLER_TOOLS_GITHUB_MIRROR_TEMPLATE` or `TAURI_BUNDLER_TOOLS_GITHUB_MIRROR` is set for a GitHub release URL, the generated `alt_url` is discarded and the original GitHub URL is returned. In networks that require the documented mirror, build-tool downloads still contact GitHub and fail; return `alt_url` here.
findings.failureMode: A user configures a GitHub mirror because github.com is unavailable or rate-limited, but bundling requests the original URL and the tool download fails.
findings.title: Configured GitHub mirrors are ignored

findings.description: `FileAssociation::name` remains optional and defaults to `ext[0]`, but plist generation now calls `expect`. Any existing association that omits `name`—including every entry in the changed example—panics while creating a macOS bundle instead of using its extension as `CFBundleTypeName`. Restore the previous extension fallback.
findings.failureMode: Running the macOS bundler for a valid config such as `{ "ext": ["png"] }` reaches `expect("File association must have a name")` and crashes.
findings.title: Keep the documented extension fallback for unnamed associations

findings.description: The new condition is inverted: every normal association has a nonempty `ext`, so its generated `CFBundleDocumentTypes` entry now omits `CFBundleTypeExtensions`. For an association with an explicit `name` (avoiding the separate unnamed-association panic), macOS no longer registers the listed extension. Insert the key when `!association.ext.is_empty()` (or unconditionally as before).
findings.failureMode: Building a macOS bundle with `fileAssociations: [{ "ext": ["png"], "name": "PNG" }]` succeeds but produces a document type without `CFBundleTypeExtensions`, so Finder/Launch Services cannot associate `.png` files with the app.
findings.title: Restore extension entries for nonempty associations

findings.description: `UTTypeConformsTo` is populated from `association.content_types`, but the newly exposed contract stores this metadata in `association.exported_type.conforms_to`. Thus `exportedType.conformsTo` is ignored (and an unrelated `contentTypes` value would be emitted as conformance instead). Use `exported_type.conforms_to` here.
findings.failureMode: With `ext: ["mydata"]`, `name` explicitly set, and `exportedType: { "identifier": "com.example.data", "conformsTo": ["public.json"] }` but no top-level `contentTypes`, bundling succeeds yet the exported declaration lacks `UTTypeConformsTo`, so macOS does not recognize the custom type as conforming to JSON.
findings.title: Read conformance types from the exported type

findings.description: A proactive firing can have `triggering_event=None`, but `triggers.act` still creates an `automation.triggered` event and passes its ID into every default `TriggeredAction`. This validator rejects that valid message, so a proactive automation that fires without a prior matching event raises validation instead of publishing any normal actions; because bucket cleanup occurs after `fire`, periodic evaluation can retry and emit state-change events repeatedly. The state-change ID is independent of the optional original event, so remove this rejection.
findings.failureMode: When a proactive automation expires without a matching/last event, `act()` constructs a `TriggeredAction` with a non-null state-change ID and null triggering event; model validation raises and no action is queued.
findings.title: Allow state-change links without a triggering event

findings.description: On the `ActionFailed` path, `related_resources` is populated with both the new `automation-triggered-event` link and the original `triggering-event`, but the emitted `prefect.automation.action.triggered` event is switched to the unaugmented private list. Thus every failed action's start event omits both source links (and the new failure-path test that looks for the automation link fails). Pass `related_resources` here, as the success path does.
findings.failureMode: When any action raises `ActionFailed`, its action-start event is emitted without the source-event relationships, breaking traceability and the added failure-event test.
findings.title: Use the augmented related resources for failed action starts

findings.description: Calling the public `Webview::delete_cookie` with an existing cookie now reaches this dispatcher and sends `SetCookie`, so the separate `DeleteCookie` match arm is never reached and the cookie is retained/re-set even though the call returns success. Change only the variant to `WebviewMessage::DeleteCookie(cookie.into_owned())`; removing the old clone is still valid because this method owns `cookie`.
findings.failureMode: For any existing cookie, invoking `Webview::delete_cookie` or `WebviewWindow::delete_cookie` returns success but performs the set operation, leaving the cookie present instead of deleting it.
findings.title: Dispatch cookie deletion as `DeleteCookie`

findings.description: The changed calls contain non-rustfmt spacing (`size.width,    size.height` at line 1317 and `position.x,position.y` at line 1321). The required `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails on exactly these two lines, so the formatting CI job rejects this revision; run rustfmt on the file.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory Rust formatting check exits 1 and reports diffs at lines 1317 and 1321, failing the merge gate.
findings.title: Format the new window-feature setters

findings.description: The changed `state !== "inherit"` condition reverses the repository argument shapes. Enabled/disabled writes now omit the required `assignedBy`; creating a user's first opt-in row therefore fails Prisma validation (and existing rows lose actor attribution), while the inherit branch reads a field that cannot exist and sends `user-undefined`. Restore the original branch direction so only inherit omits attribution.
findings.failureMode: A normal first-time enabled/disabled user feature mutation reaches Prisma without the required `assignedBy` field and fails; the package also no longer type-checks and its unit suite fails.
findings.title: Restore the user-state branch direction

findings.description: The new predicate is inverted: when a user-scoped opt-in feature is globally enabled, `listFeaturesForUser` now removes it, while globally disabled features are returned. Once `OPT_IN_FEATURES` contains a user-scoped feature, the user settings query therefore shows the wrong feature set. Filter on `state.globalEnabled` as before.
findings.failureMode: A globally enabled user-scoped feature disappears from `/settings/my-account/features`, while a globally disabled one can be returned.
findings.title: Keep globally enabled user features

findings.description: Dropping `await` makes this tRPC mutation return `{ success: true }` before scope validation or the repository write completes. For a feature that is not user-scoped, the intended `BadRequest` rejection is detached and the client receives success; database failures are likewise not reported and can become unhandled rejections. Await the service call, as the team/org mutations do.
findings.failureMode: A rejected or failed user feature update is reported to the client as successful, while the write has not completed or never occurs.
findings.title: Await the user feature-state mutation

findings.description: The mandatory Biome formatter rejects changed lines in config.ts (the three new scope constants), FeatureOptInService.test.ts (new mock entries and feature-id expectations), FeatureOptInService.ts (the widened union), and IFeatureOptInService.ts (the matching union). Thus the formatting gate exits nonzero; apply the repository formatter to those changed files.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory Biome format check exits nonzero on the PR's changed files.
findings.title: Format the changed TypeScript files with Biome

findings.description: `ASM_EVENT_IMPORT_START` duplicates the implementation-supplied array before checking `num_ranges`. A malformed array with `num_ranges == -1` makes `slotRangeArrayCreate` perform wrapped-size allocation arithmetic and then makes `memcpy` use an enormous size; an oversized positive count similarly attempts an unbounded allocation. Thus the new validation path can crash Redis rather than return `C_ERR`, precisely for the malformed external input it is meant to reject. Check `arg` and the count bounds before copying.
findings.failureMode: An alternative cluster implementation passing an invalid range-array count to ASM_EVENT_IMPORT_START crashes or OOM-aborts the Redis server.
findings.title: Bounds-check external ranges before duplicating them

findings.description: `total_ranges` is assigned but never read. The required `make REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror"` build fails while compiling `cluster_asm.c` with `-Wunused-variable`; remove the local (or use it as the loop bound).
findings.failureMode: The repository's required warnings-as-errors build fails at compile time for every build of cluster_asm.c.
findings.title: Remove the unused `total_ranges` local

findings.description: Normalization runs before the per-range `start <= end` check, so an invalid range can be merged away and accepted. For example `[0,0] [1,0]` satisfies the adjacency test and collapses to `[0,0]`; on a stable destination that does not own slot 0, `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT 0 0 1 0` then starts a migration for slot 0 instead of rejecting the reversed second range. Validate original entries before compaction.
findings.failureMode: A malformed multi-range import request is accepted and silently migrates fewer slots than the caller supplied.
findings.title: Validate each range before merging it

findings.description: When normalization rejects a parsed range (for example `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT 200 100` or overlapping ranges), this branch now frees `err` instead of passing it to `addReplyErrorSds`. `parseSlotRangesOrReply` returns NULL and its callers immediately return, so the command produces no RESP reply and the client waits indefinitely; keep sending the generated validation error before returning.
findings.failureMode: A command with numeric but invalid/overlapping slot ranges hangs without a server response instead of receiving the documented error.
findings.title: Return validation errors to the command client

findings.description: These calls can change each array's `num_ranges`, but the only length check occurs before them. For example, `[0-0,1-1]` and `[0-1,3-3]` both enter with two ranges; the first normalizes to one range, the second stays at two, and the loop compares only `[0-1]` before incorrectly returning 1 and ignoring slot 3. Conversely, an adjacent two-range array and its one-range canonical form return 0 before normalization. Normalize first and then compare the resulting counts.
findings.failureMode: The exported equality operation returns true for different slot sets (or false for equivalent representations), causing callers to associate a slot update/retry with the wrong task when noncanonical arrays reach it.
findings.title: Compare normalized range counts before contents

findings.description: Both new helpers have external linkage despite being used only in their defining files: `asmCountKeysInSlots` here and `slotRangeArraySortAndMerge` at `src/cluster.c:1860` (also exposed at `src/cluster.h:187`). This violates the repository's mandatory static-storage rule for internal helpers and exports collision-prone symbols; declare both `static` and remove the header declaration.
findings.failureMode: Production objects export unintended global helper symbols, creating duplicate-symbol link failures if another compilation unit uses either internal helper name.
findings.title: Keep the new helper functions file-local

findings.description: Using `<` skips the configured band at exact thresholds. With a prior `csd_email_count` of 1,000, 5,000, or 100,000, the service returns 1,500, 8,750, or 200,000 instead of the documented and newly asserted 1,250, 7,500, or 175,000. This makes the production warmup ramp too aggressive and the isolated unit suite fails at the first such boundary; use an inclusive comparison for these upper bounds.
findings.failureMode: An email whose highest prior CSD count is exactly 1,000, 5,000, or 100,000 receives the next scale factor rather than the intended current-band factor, yielding an excessive warmup limit.
findings.title: Keep each threshold endpoint in its configured scale band

findings.description: Changing the cutoff from `created_at:<today` to `created_at:<=today` contradicts this method's excluding-today contract. A send whose `created_at` equals the day's midnight boundary is now eligible and can make a second newsletter ramp again instead of holding the daily warmup limit. The isolated changed unit suite also fails deterministically on the filter assertion. Restore the strict `<today` cutoff while retaining `findPage`.
findings.failureMode: When an earlier same-day email has a timestamp at the day's comparison boundary, it can be included as warmup history, causing another same-day limit increase; the committed unit test also fails on every run.
findings.title: Exclude today's sends from the historical maximum

findings.description: The new `>=` branch intercepts `lastCount === 400000` before the 2× threshold can run, returning 475,000 rather than the specified 800,000. The changed progression test explicitly asserts 800,000 at this boundary, so once earlier boundary failures are fixed it still fails, and production sites hitting exactly 400k get the wrong next-send warmup limit. Make high-volume start above the inclusive 400k band.
findings.failureMode: A sender with exactly 400,000 messages in its highest prior CSD send is capped to 475,000 rather than receiving the intended 2× limit of 800,000.
findings.title: Do not apply the high-volume cap at exactly 400k

findings.description: The new `count != null` comparison violates the mandatory strict-equality rule and `yarn lint:types` reports `Expected '!==' and instead saw '!='`. The intended nullish fallback needs explicit strict checks for `null` and `undefined`; as committed, the repository lint gate fails.
findings.failureMode: The changed service fails the TypeScript lint check on the loose inequality operator.
findings.title: Use strict null checks

findings.description: The success branch resolves `default` to `TanStackDevtoolsWrapper` (inferred as `() => JSX.Element`), while this catch branch resolves `() => null`. TypeScript therefore rejects the `lazy` loader (`TS2322: null is not assignable to Element`), so the required web type-check fails on every web change. Return a fallback with a compatible JSX-element return type (for example an empty fragment), explicitly widen the component type, or rethrow the import error.
findings.failureMode: The required `tsgo --noEmit` web check fails at this lazy import, blocking the change.
findings.title: Return a compatible lazy fallback component

findings.description: On a non-English locale in development, every suspended React Scan import renders the hardcoded English text `Loading devtools...`; because the loader sits outside `I18nServer`, this is an untranslated user-visible flash. The repository requires frontend-facing strings to come from i18n, so use a translated fallback inside the provider or a non-text/null fallback.
findings.failureMode: A localized development page displays an English-only loading message while the React Scan chunk loads.
findings.title: Localize or hide the loading fallback

findings.description: When the React Scan chunk fails to load in development, this catch executes `console.error`, emitting an unmanaged browser-console message instead of using the repository's approved reporting path. The mandatory frontend rule prohibits console statements outside tests, and the statement is also retained in the production layout chunk; remove it or route the failure through the approved logger/error reporter.
findings.failureMode: A development-time chunk load failure produces forbidden unmanaged console output, with the debug statement retained in production assets.
findings.title: Remove the new console call

findings.description: This change replaces the required file-scoped namespace with a block-scoped declaration. The owning project's warnings-as-errors build now emits IDE0161 at this line and stops before tests execute; restore `namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits;` and remove the added namespace braces.
findings.failureMode: Building `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Tests.csproj` fails with IDE0161 at line 10.
findings.title: Restore the file-scoped namespace

findings.description: The test renders `GenericComponent<int>`, but both marker assertions use `GenericComponent<string>` (lines 837-838). The assembly comparison happens to be equal, while the type-name comparison deterministically fails on the correctly emitted Int32 specialization. Compare both values against `typeof(GenericComponent<int>)`.
findings.failureMode: The Endpoints suite runs 482 tests and fails exactly `CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ClientMode`: expected the String specialization but received the correctly serialized Int32 specialization.
findings.title: Assert the rendered generic specialization

findings.description: Both generic markers are serialized with the same `ServerComponentInvocationSequence`, so `SerializeInvocation` assigns sequence 0 then 1, exactly as the adjacent existing multiple-marker test expects. The new assertion expects 0 for the second descriptor, causing this test to fail; it must expect 1.
findings.failureMode: With warnings downgraded so the suite can run, `CanParseMultipleMarkersForClosedGenericComponents` fails at line 144: expected 0, actual 1.
findings.title: Expect the incremented second marker sequence

findings.description: All four newly added test methods return `Task` and use `async`, but their names omit the repository-mandated `Async` suffix (also at lines 739, 778, and 817). Rename them with `Async` so the added C# methods satisfy the async API naming requirement.
findings.failureMode: The four new asynchronous C# methods fail the repository's mandatory async-method naming compliance gate.
findings.title: Suffix the new async test methods

findings.description: When JWT mode is enabled, `_generateToken()` returns `{token, exp}`, but this assignment stores that whole object in `_serverToken`. `getToken()` therefore returns an object as `token`: the admin client explicitly rejects non-string tokens and disables every Tinybird query, while server-side callers interpolate it as `Bearer [object Object]`. Assign `tokenData.token` here so JWT-backed analytics continues to load.
findings.failureMode: With `workspaceId` and `adminToken` configured, the Analytics UI receives no valid token and runs no Tinybird queries, and server-side stats requests fail authentication.
findings.title: Cache the signed token string, not the metadata object

findings.description: The newly documented first step cannot install anything: `@tinybird/cli` returns 404 from the npm registry, while this repository already provides `yarn tb:install` to install the Tinybird CLI. The second command also contradicts the mandatory Yarn v1 workflow. Following this block stops before the Tinybird tests can run; document `yarn tb:install` and `yarn docker:dev:analytics` instead.
findings.failureMode: A developer following the new local-test instructions gets an npm package-not-found error and cannot start the Tinybird test environment.
findings.title: Use the repository's working Tinybird setup commands

findings.description: Adding `BundleType::Flatpak` makes the existing exhaustive `impl From<BundleType> for PackageType` in `tauri-bundler` non-exhaustive because that match only handles the seven previous variants. Any workspace/CLI build that compiles `tauri-bundler` now fails with E0004; add the corresponding `PackageType` and conversion/bundling support, or do not expose this variant yet.
findings.failureMode: Compiling tauri-bundler after the new enum variant is added fails due to a non-exhaustive match.
findings.title: Add Flatpak handling to the bundler conversion

findings.description: `config.rs` is the source for the checked-in configuration schemas, but the shipped `config.schema.json` still lists only the old bundle values and none of the generated schema files contains `flatpak`. The CLI loads that file for JSON/JSON5 configs and exits with status 1 on validation errors, so a config using the newly accepted `bundle.targets: "flatpak"` is rejected before deserialization. Regenerate and commit all configuration schema artifacts.
findings.failureMode: The CLI exits with status 1 for a JSON/JSON5 configuration using the newly accepted Flatpak target because its embedded schema is stale.
findings.title: Regenerate the configuration schemas

findings.description: `BundleType`'s schema is declared `rename_all = "lowercase"`, and `Serialize` delegates to this `Display` implementation, but the new arm emits `"Flatpak"`. Serializing a config with this target therefore produces a value that does not match the generated schema's `"flatpak"` enum value (and differs from every other target). Return `"flatpak"` here.
findings.failureMode: Serializing a configuration that selects Flatpak emits schema-invalid output (`Flatpak` rather than `flatpak`).
findings.title: Serialize Flatpak with the lowercase schema value

findings.description: When an invalid `Tauri.toml` is parsed with `config-toml`, this maps the TOML parser failure to `ConfigError::FormatJson` and synthesizes a JSON error. The displayed diagnostic incorrectly says the TOML file is JSON, and callers matching the documented `FormatToml` variant no longer receive it. `toml` 0.9.4's `from_str` still returns `toml::de::Error` (as the unchanged v1 parser also demonstrates), so retain the `FormatToml` mapping and box the error as before.
findings.failureMode: An invalid Tauri.toml returns the wrong public error variant and an incorrect JSON diagnostic.
findings.title: Preserve TOML parse errors as `FormatToml`

findings.description: This added public configuration target is user-facing functionality, but the diff adds no `.changes/*.md` covector entry. That violates the repository's release-versioning mandate, so the Flatpak addition would be omitted from the generated changelog/version bump unless a change file is added.
findings.failureMode: Release tooling has no change record for the newly exposed Flatpak bundle target, so the release changelog/version plan omits it.
findings.title: Add a change file for the new Flatpak target

findings.description: The new public variant is not added to the `BundleConfig::targets` documentation, which still says the supported targets are only `deb`, `rpm`, `appimage`, `nsis`, `msi`, `app`, and `dmg`. Generated Rust/API documentation therefore tells users that the newly accepted Flatpak value is unsupported. Update that public field's supported-values list together with the variant.
findings.failureMode: Published API documentation omits the newly supported Flatpak target and gives users an incorrect supported-values list.
findings.title: Document Flatpak in `BundleConfig::targets`

findings.description: `ios::command` now resolves and caches app paths before dispatching every subcommand. The hidden `xcode-script` subcommand intentionally changes from Xcode's generated-project working directory back to the app directory at the start of `xcode_script::command`; previously path resolution happened only after that adjustment. Invoking the built CLI from a normal `<src-tauri>/gen/apple` directory with no `TAURI_APP_PATH` now panics before the script can correct the cwd (reproduced with exit 101). Resolve inside the individual branches, or let `xcode-script` resolve after its cwd setup.
findings.failureMode: The generated iOS Xcode build script panics at startup when launched from gen/apple, preventing Xcode builds.
findings.title: Resolve paths only after Xcode script changes cwd

findings.description: When the billing batch contains a plan that fails `SubscriptionPlan` validation (for example, one missing `expiration_date`), this branch inserts that tenant into a return value declared and consumed as `dict[str, SubscriptionPlan]`. The added unit test explicitly expects the invalid tenant to be absent, so it fails at `len(result) == 2`; production/cache callers can likewise receive and cache JSON `null`, then error when indexing the plan. Remove this assignment and continue past the invalid item.
findings.failureMode: A malformed plan in an otherwise successful billing response is returned and cached as `None`, failing the added unit test and causing downstream plan access to error.
findings.title: Skip invalid plans instead of returning `None`

findings.description: `SubscriptionPlan` is a `TypedDict`, whose class body may contain only type annotations. The required backend style workflow runs basedpyright, and the check now fails at this method with `TypedDict classes can contain only type annotations`, so the PR cannot pass CI. Remove this ignored runtime method (or use a normal/Pydantic model if behavior is required).
findings.failureMode: Running the required strict basedpyright check fails on the changed `__str__` definition, blocking validation of the backend.
findings.title: Remove the method from `SubscriptionPlan`

findings.description: This repository can initialize `redis_client` as `RedisCluster`, but the generated keys use tenant-specific hashes and therefore normally map to different slots. Redis Cluster rejects a multi-key `MGET` unless every key shares one slot; the broad handler then treats every request as a miss, so repeated bulk calls always hit billing and this cache provides no load reduction in supported cluster deployments. Use a cluster-aware per-slot/pipelined read, or deliberately add a common hash tag to the cache keys.
findings.failureMode: With `REDIS_USE_CLUSTERS` and at least two tenant IDs in different hash slots, every cache read raises a cross-slot error and falls back to the billing API, making the new cache nonfunctional and potentially overloading billing.
findings.title: Avoid cross-slot `MGET` in Redis Cluster mode
